body:
COUNTER-ATTACK ACCEPTED — FINAL VERDICT (leak prevention prioritized): split the PUBLIC AUDIENCE/STAGE surface onto a separate origin, while keeping SETUP+CONTROLLER+PRESENTER/NOTES together on one trusted origin. Use WSS as the only presentation-state/data plane. My earlier all-UI-same-origin recommendation optimized convenience, not least privilege.

Yes, the trusted setup/controller can call `getScreenDetails()` on its own origin, compute target coordinates, then `window.open('https://stage.example/...', name, left/top/width/height)` to place a cross-origin audience window. Window placement does not require the opened URL to be same-origin. The retained cross-origin WindowProxy can ordinarily expose `focus`, `close`, `closed`, `blur`, and `postMessage`, but not DOM/state/functions. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/opener and https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open

However, choose explicitly between two security modes:
A) Recommended strict isolation: audience sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: noopener-allow-popups` or otherwise severs opener (`noopener`). Then the returned WindowProxy reports `closed === true`; controller cannot reliably focus/close/liveness-check it. Use WSS presence/heartbeat for liveness, and audience-local controls/user close. This best prevents either side scripting the other. Evidence: Window.open says a new browsing-context group severs references and returned `closed` becomes true: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open ; COOP details: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
B) Moderate isolation: compatible COOP (`unsafe-none` on audience; if controller needs isolation, `same-origin-allow-popups`) retains the restricted cross-origin handle, so controller can focus/close/check `closed`. This still isolates cookies/localStorage/SW/DOM, but keeps an opener relationship and allows limited navigation/postMessage surface. Since both origins are ours, it may be acceptable, but it is not the maximum-leak-prevention choice.

Fullscreen caveat is material: controller CANNOT call `audienceWindow.document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()` cross-origin. Fullscreen requires transient user activation in the document making the request. A WSS message or controller click does not confer activation to the stage document. Therefore strict cross-origin stage must show a one-time local `Enter fullscreen` click (then call `requestFullscreen()` itself), or settle for sized window placement. Targeted `{screen}` fullscreen also must be requested by that document and is Chromium/experimental. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestFullscreen and https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/

Security boundary details:
- `stage.example.com`: no auth cookies, no user/session secrets, no microphone, no AI prompts/notes, no control APIs; narrowly scoped stage-only SW/cache; connect WSS with a short-lived, single-presentation, audience-read-only capability token (avoid broadly scoped cookies; if cookies exist, never `Domain=.example.com`).
- `app.example.com`: setup/controller/presenter notes, microphone, AI/session data, trusted SW/storage.
- WSS server validates role/capability and never trusts origin alone; stage receives only rendered slide state/assets and presentation timing.
- Use server relay as source of truth even if a restricted opener handle is retained.

Thus: SEPARATE audience origin is the right security-first design. Keep trusted setup/controller/presenter same-origin with each other. Treat focus/closed as optional convenience only; strict COOP forfeits them. Require an audience-local fullscreen gesture and design a clear one-click handoff.
summary: Security-first verdict favors isolated audience origin
